step1_summary: Chief complaint: “Struggling to breathe” after a presumed wasp/bee sting that occurred only a few minutes ago.

Symptoms: • Onset: immediately after sting • Duration: ongoing for several minutes • Character: mild sense of dyspnoea, slight lip tingling/swelling, ‘weird’ tongue sensation, local arm rash/redness with puncture mark • Severity: patient able to speak full sentences; no stridor heard on video • Aggravating/alleviating: none tried yet, no medications yet, anxiety present
Past medical history: eczema; occasional anxiety/panic episodes; no prior anaphylaxis; never prescribed an EpiPen
Medications/allergies: no regular meds; allergic to penicillin; has not taken antihistamine yet
Family/social history: no relevant family illnesses reported; 27-year-old male computer scientist; lives alone with a cat; no known environmental or food allergies

Vital signs/exam findings (video): normal conversational speech; breathing appears normal; lips not visibly swollen; oral cavity/throat look normal; sting site shows mild erythema with puncture, no overt swelling or heat

V: Angioedema secondary to complement dysfunction (hereditary or acquired): rapid swelling can compromise airway, but no family history or recurrent episodes
I: Early cellulitis at sting site: local redness could evolve into infection
Venom-induced local inflammatory reaction: typical after stings
N: None directly relevant; no mass or malignancy fits the acute presentation
D: Panic/anxiety episode precipitating sensation of dyspnoea
I2: Toxic reaction to wasp/bee venom (non-IgE mediated ‘toxic envenomation’)
C: Hereditary angioedema (overlaps with V as above; included for completeness)
A: IgE-mediated anaphylaxis / systemic allergic reaction to insect venom
T: Traumatic local reaction from the sting itself (mechanical injury + venom)

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Localized allergic reaction to insect sting (uncomplicated venom-induced inflammation)
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Most stings produce immediate localized erythema, mild edema and discomfort without systemic involvement; exam shows only local redness, no systemic compromise

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Early IgE-mediated anaphylaxis / systemic allergic reaction
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Timing (minutes after sting), patient-reported lip tingling and dyspnoea raise concern, though objective signs are currently absent; must remain on differential because reactions can progress rapidly

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Anxiety/panic attack triggered by sting event
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Patient has history of anxiety; subjective ‘difficulty breathing’ without objective findings is common in panic; reassurance quickly improved comfort

step3_ranked_ddx.diagnosis: Cellulitis/early skin infection at sting site
step3_ranked_ddx.explanation: Localized erythema could evolve into infection but onset is too rapid (minutes) and no warmth or spreading erythema yet
Large doses or multiple stings can cause systemic toxicity; only one sting reported with minimal findings

supporting_evidence: Erythematous blotchy rash confined to sting site
Puncture mark consistent with insect sting
No objective respiratory compromise or hypotension
opposing_evidence: Subjective lip tingling and dyspnoea could indicate systemic spread
Normal speech and appearance on video
No visible swelling, stridor, urticaria elsewhere, or vital-sign abnormalities

supporting_evidence: Subjective breathlessness disproportionate to objective findings
Reassurance from physician markedly reduced concern
opposing_evidence: Clear trigger (sting) with local cutaneous findings suggests physiologic component
Lip tingling not typical for isolated panic
Extremely rapid onset (minutes) argues against infection
No warmth, spreading erythema, or systemic signs

supporting_evidence: Insect venom can produce systemic effects
opposing_evidence: Only single sting, mild localized findings, no systemic symptoms like vomiting, headache, hypotension
